thread.title: Nike Beats Q3 Views, Sees 'Significant' North America Trend Reversal

author: ELAINE LOW
title: Nike Beats Q3 Views, Sees 'Significant' North America Trend Reversal
text:
Nike ( NKE ) topped fiscal Q3 forecasts after the close Thursday and signaled a recent sales slump in North America is ending, helping offset fears of a trade war sparked by President Trump's tariffs.
X Estimates : A 23.5% slide to 52 cents in per-share profit. Analysts see revenue rising 4.9% to $8.84 billion, according to Zacks Investment Research.
Results : EPS of 68 cents, excluding tax-related charges, on revenue of $8.98 billion. North America revenue fell 6% to $3.57 billion with apparel flat and footwear down 8%. Europe, Middle East and Africa revenue jumped 19% to $2.3 billion. Greater China revenue surged 24% to $1.34 billion. Asia Pacific and Latin America revenue grew 13% to $1.27 billion.
"Nike's Consumer Direct Offense drove strong double-digit growth across our international geographies, led by Greater China," said Chairman and CEO Mark Parker in a statement. "As we close Q3, we now see a significant reversal of trend in North America, as momentum accelerates through the scaling of new innovation platforms and differentiated NIKE Consumer Experiences expand across the marketplace."
Stock : Nike jumped 7.1% late. Shares closed down 2.9% at 64.42 on the stock market today , breaching their 50-day moving average as the Trump administration unveiled tariffs against China , which has been a top growth driver for Nike. Rival Under Armour ( UAA ) fell 1.4%. Major Nike retailer Foot Locker ( FL ) sank 4.3%.

Please contact customer service CLOSE North America revenue has been in focus, as sales have slumped while rival Adidas ( ADDYY ) has been gaining share on Nike's home turf and turned in double-digit growth during the holiday quarter .
Adidas North America chief Mark King told Investor's Business Daily last week that its growth in the family channel — at stores such as Kohl's ( KSS ) and DSW ( DSW ) — and at Dick's Sporting Goods ( DKS ), where its training apparel is sold, are strong.
But Nike's continued strong performance in China also underscores a vulnerability as Trump has directed relatively heavy economic fire toward China. Nike has echoed concerns from trade groups representing Walmart ( WMT ), Apple ( AAPL ), Best Buy ( BBY ) and other retailers warning that tariffs would raise prices for American consumers.
Meanwhile, CEO Parker must grapple with other recent headlines. An informal survey about inappropriate behavior had been circulated by female Nike employees, reported the Wall Street Journal earlier in the week.
The news followed the resignation of No. 2 executive and Nike Brand President Trevor Edwards and the exit of exec Jayme Martin, who was forced out amid complaints of misconduct.
